_comment: WHY THIS GATE NEEDS ONE: it is a prerequisite of `make verify`, a gate that lets
work THROUGH, and nothing downstream re-derives it. A blind version prints the same
'ok - N relative link(s) ... resolve' line over a tree whose links have rotted, which
is exactly the state #1413 found by hand.
limits: Covers inline relative markdown links resolving to an existing file, relative to the linking document's own directory, outside fenced blocks and inline code. It says nothing about URLs, #fragments (the heading is never checked), image links, reference-style definitions, or backtick path mentions, none of which the gate examines. The real tree's verdict is the gate's own run under `make verify`. The membership floor is lowered to 1 here because a case tree is small; the real-tree default (100) is pinned by tests/test_check_md_relative_links.py. UNAVAILABLE is declared for a missing git only.

cases.name: bad-dead-link
cases.why: README.md links to guide.md, which does not exist. The one failure the gate exists for.

cases.name: bad-dead-link-from-subdir
cases.why: docs/guide.md links to ../plan.md, which does not exist, while the top-level README's own link is live. Pins resolution relative to the LINKING file's directory, and that a dead link outside the top level is still found - the shape of every link #1413 fixed.

cases.name: good-live-links
cases.why: Live links in both directions, a #fragment on a live link, a URL, a bare anchor, and a dead target written only inside inline code and a fenced block. Separates a working gate from one wedged at 'fail', and from one that reads examples as links.

cases.name: unknown-no-links
cases.why: A tracked document whose only links are a URL and inline code. Zero relative links examined must not read as 'every link resolves'.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the coverage before #1413 - relative links checked in CLAUDE.md and nowhere else. No case carries a CLAUDE.md, so it reports GOOD on both BAD cases (blind, as required) and agrees with the gate on the GOOD case.
